routes.description: Establish that belief in the biblical God is rational through a cumulative case from scientific intelligibility, human rationality, objective morality, historical claims about Jesus, and the resources of Christian theism for addressing suffering, hope, meaning, and justice.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if these considerations jointly provide adequate grounds for biblical theism and its account of the evidence remains viable against naturalistic explanations, the problem of suffering, and objections to the resurrection and scripture.

motionBridge.description: Show that the cumulative scientific, philosophical, moral, and historical case warrants belief in the biblical God as rational.

centralBridges.description: Show that a rational creator explains cosmic intelligibility, fine-tuning, reliable cognition, and the possibility of science better than mindless ultimate reality.
Show that objective moral obligation, equality, and intrinsic human value require or are best grounded in a transcendent personal source.
Show that historical evidence concerning Jesus and the resurrection supports the specifically biblical identification of the creator and makes Christian belief testable.
Show that suffering does not defeat biblical theism because Christ's participation in suffering, resurrection, compensation, final justice, and future life sustain a coherent response.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Defend an uncreated God as a coherent explanatory terminus and distinguish divine agency from a gap-filling substitute for scientific mechanisms.
Connect divine intention, forgiveness, transformed life, and creation in God's image to personal meaning and human worth.

routes.description: Establish that belief in the biblical God is not rational because naturalistic explanations make the divine hypothesis unnecessary, secular accounts can support reason and morality, suffering conflicts with the claimed divine attributes, and the evidence for Jesus's resurrection and scriptural authority is inadequate.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if biblical theism lacks sufficient explanatory or historical support, or if suffering and problems in its historical and scriptural claims outweigh its proposed grounds, while secular naturalism remains adequate for reason, ethics, meaning, and hope.

motionBridge.description: Show that the available scientific, philosophical, moral, and historical considerations do not warrant belief in the biblical God.

centralBridges.description: Show that cosmology and evolution can explain origins, order, apparent design, consciousness, and rational capacities without adding a divine hypothesis.
Show that objective moral conclusions and impartial concern for others can be rationally defended without divine commands or a theistic foundation.
Show that extensive undeserved human and animal suffering is improbable under an omniscient, omnipotent, and wholly good biblical creator.
Show that late and interested resurrection testimony, alternative explanations, disputed prophecy, and scriptural defects cannot support Jesus's divinity or biblical authority.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Show that exempting God from causal explanation supplies no clear advantage over treating reality or the universe as uncreated.
Show that finite hope, self-created purpose, and efforts to reduce suffering remain available without immortality or divinely assigned purpose.

sections.title: Cosmos, Science, and Explanatory Need
sections.rationale: This issue tests whether cosmic origins, intelligibility, fine-tuning, and apparent design support a creator or are adequately addressed by cosmology, evolution, and an uncreated natural reality.

sections.title: Human Reason, Consciousness, and Naturalism
sections.rationale: This issue determines whether evolved cognition undermines confidence in reason or instead supplies a viable natural account of consciousness and truth-directed rational capacities.

sections.title: Morality, Equality, and Human Value
sections.rationale: This issue examines whether objective morality, impartial obligation, equality, and intrinsic human worth require the biblical God or admit an independent secular foundation.

sections.title: Suffering, Hope, and Final Justice
sections.rationale: This issue weighs undeserved natural and moral suffering against Christian appeals to divine participation, future compensation, resurrection hope, and final justice.

sections.title: Jesus, Resurrection, and Scriptural Authority
sections.rationale: This issue governs the bridge from generic theism to the biblical God by testing the historical basis of the resurrection, Jesus's identity, disputed prophecy, miracles, and scriptural reliability.

sections.title: Purpose, Afterlife, and Transformed Life
sections.rationale: This issue compares divinely grounded meaning, forgiveness, immortality, and transformed life with finite secular hope, self-created purpose, and concerns about wish-fulfillment.
